correctness.rationale: The append-one-letter partition of two-deletion descendants proves the deterministic formula for any alphabet, with the two length-two bases covered. The two-state coefficient polynomial accounts for each new letter and return choice. For independent uniformly sampled letters, centered boundary-change variables are independent; conditional return indicators have constant one-over-(q-1) success probabilities. The exact polynomial second moment follows from orthogonality of degree-one and degree-two centered monomials and conditional total variance; all formulas include n=2. The Gaussian limit uses a Bernoulli CLT and L2-negligibility of quadratic and return noise. Direct exhaustive descendant sets, run formula, edge enumeration and independent transfer DP agree on 33 complete parameter cases; symbolic moments agree on 60 cases. Finite experiments only corroborate the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The accepted contribution is the exact nonbinary full distribution and its transfer/variance/limit; the already-published binary variance is expressly not claimed new. The strongest published overlap proves only the q=2 variance, while the 2003 run formula is binary. The 2021 primary paper focuses on binary deletion-ball intersections and maxima. Nonbinary return-to-prior-symbol probabilities require genuine additional terms. Searches on exact domain, equivalent terms, alphabet parameter and matrix reduction found no implication covering the all-q distribution. Residual unindexed-equivalent risk is recorded.
residual_risks: Older differently named q-ary run-statistic or generating-function literature might imply the two-state distribution and was not identified by search.
The 2026 q-ary intersection manuscript could only be scope-checked from its accessible abstract; no full-text NOT_COVERING conclusion is made for it.
Finite code does not prove infinite claims; a separately reconstructed induction, algebraic variance and CLT are the actual proof.

value.rationale: A complete exact source-volume distribution is a natural invariant for q-ary two-deletion channels, refining the previously studied binary variance and extremal volumes. The two-state transfer handles every alphabet and length, not a single arbitrary cutoff, and captures the new return/nonreturn transition mechanism that only appears for q>=3. A closed variance polynomial and precise Gaussian scale demonstrate the typical irregularity of deletion balls. Such a distribution may inform sphere-volume weighted coding estimates, though no unproved downstream code-rate claim is made.
